paths.name: electron
paths.message: The web app is the renderer and runs in a plain browser too. Reach the desktop through the window.gram bridge, whose shape is in @gram/contracts, never Electron itself.

patterns.message: This code runs in the browser renderer, where Node has no modules. Ask the server over the API, or the desktop through the window.gram bridge.

The web app runs in the browser and only talks to the server and the shell over their contracts. Its package.json names what it may depend on (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): @gram/contracts, @gram/themes. Move the shared piece down into one of those (shapes go in @gram/contracts), or put this code in the package that already owns the dependency.

paths.name: electron
paths.message: Contracts and themes are shared by the browser, the server and Electron alike, so they import no runtime. Keep runtime code in the package that runs it.

patterns.message: Contracts and themes are loaded in the browser too, where Node has no modules. Keep this here as a pure shape or value, and do the Node work in @gram/server or @gram/git.

Contracts and themes are the bottom of the graph and import nothing in the workspace. Its package.json names what it may depend on (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): nothing in the workspace. Move the shared piece down into one of those (shapes go in @gram/contracts), or put this code in the package that already owns the dependency.
A package never imports an app: apps depend on packages, not the other way round. Move what both need into the package (or into @gram/contracts if it is a shared shape).

paths.message: Native Electron is main-process only: keep it in @gram/shell (core, electron, modules) or apps/desktop/src/main. Here, take what you need as a parameter or through a shell module, so this code stays usable outside Electron.

A package never imports an app: apps depend on packages, not the other way round. Move what both need into the package (or into @gram/contracts if it is a shared shape).

patterns.message: The server runs as its own Node process, with or without the desktop. Its package.json names what it may depend on (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): @gram/agents, @gram/contracts, @gram/git. Move the shared piece down into one of those (shapes go in @gram/contracts), or put this code in the package that already owns the dependency.
A package never imports an app: apps depend on packages, not the other way round. Move what both need into the package (or into @gram/contracts if it is a shared shape).

The shell is the Electron layer and reaches the server over its API, not its source. Its package.json names what it may depend on (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): @gram/contracts, @gram/git. Move the shared piece down into one of those (shapes go in @gram/contracts), or put this code in the package that already owns the dependency.
A package never imports an app: apps depend on packages, not the other way round. Move what both need into the package (or into @gram/contracts if it is a shared shape).

A sandboxed preload can load nothing but `electron`, so this bundle may bring in values only from `electron` and the shell's preload-safe entries: @gram/shell/channels, @gram/shell/preload and @gram/shell/window-arg (packages/shell/src/entries.test.ts holds them to it). Import types with `import type`; anything that reads files, runs a command or needs Node goes in apps/desktop/src/main behind a channel, and the preload asks for it with ipcRenderer.invoke.
The desktop's main process loads the web app as a page, it never imports it. Shapes both sides use go in @gram/contracts; the page reaches main through the window.gram bridge.

The server runs in its own process, which main starts (main/server-host.ts) and talks to over the API, so agent and server code never load into the Electron main process. From @gram/server, main may import only its light entries: @gram/server/logging, @gram/server/updates and @gram/server/host/launch-args. Ask the server over its API, or add a light export to packages/server/package.json for a pure helper.
